candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — provide client nutrition through tube feedings
candidate.educational_objective: Reduce aspiration risk during gastric tube feeding by maintaining head-of-bed elevation about 30–45 degrees when not contraindicated.

options.A: Pause the feeding only during sleep and keep the client nearly supine, because continuous enteral nutrition is safest when abdominal pressure is minimized.
options.B: Reposition the client and maintain head-of-bed elevation at about 30 to 45 degrees, while continuing the other prescribed aspiration-prevention measures.
options.C: Keep the head of the bed at 10 degrees and increase the feeding rate, because a shorter feeding duration reduces exposure to aspiration risk.
options.D: Turn the client fully onto one side with the head of the bed flat, because lateral positioning provides the same aspiration protection as elevation.

candidate.rationale: For adults receiving tube feeding, aspiration-prevention practice includes maintaining head-of-bed elevation at 30 to 45 degrees unless contraindicated, along with ongoing feeding-tube and gastrointestinal tolerance assessment. Keeping the client nearly supine or simply changing feeding speed does not provide equivalent protection.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For a tube-fed adult at aspiration risk without a contraindication, maintain head-of-bed elevation about 30–45 degrees as part of aspiration prevention.

candidate.stem: A client receiving continuous gastric tube feeding has slid down in bed so the head of the bed is elevated only 10 degrees. There is no medical contraindication to elevation. Which nursing action best reduces aspiration risk?
